blockDiagramAnalysis: SPI register interface feeds a control register and a 12-bit DAC code register into a single-channel output driver; a status register reports busy/over-range; a device ID register identifies the part.
memoryMapAnalysis: 8-bit register addresses, 16-bit register data. CTRL at 0x00 holds ENABLE and RANGE_SEL. DAC_CODE at 0x01 holds a right-justified 12-bit code in bits 0:11; bits 12:15 are reserved. STATUS at 0x02 is read-only with BUSY and OVERRANGE flags. DEVICE_ID at 0x0F is a fixed identity value.

registers.name: CTRL
registers.description: Output enable and voltage range select.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.description: 1 = DAC output driver active; 0 = output held high-impedance.

registers.name: DAC_CODE
registers.description: Right-justified 12-bit DAC code commanding the output level.
registers.writeSideEffect: Updates the commanded analog output level when ENABLE is set; the new code is observable through the model's output getter.

fields.name: CODE
fields.description: 12-bit DAC code, 0x000 = output low rail, 0xFFF = output full-scale.

fields.name: BUSY
fields.description: 1 while the output driver is still settling to a newly written code.

fields.name: OVERRANGE
fields.description: 1 if a commanded code is out of range for the selected RANGE_SEL.

timingNotes: The model should resolve BUSY synchronously (treat the settling time as instantaneous for simulation purposes) since no settling-time value is specified.
A DAC_CODE write while ENABLE is clear still updates CODE and the output getter, but the commanded level is not considered driven onto the physical output until ENABLE is set.
behavioralNotes: This is a synthetic example actuator, not a real silicon part; evidence for the generated CoreModel binding must still come from the configured CoreModel library's SPI examples.

Expose the commanded output through a getter (e.g. get_output_code()/get_output_enabled()) so a host harness can observe what the device was told to drive, matching the sensor pattern of a setter used to inject input.
